title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
description: Ten current or scheduled Penn-area cultural activities whose supporting pages state that participation or admission is free.

cards.title: See contemporary art at the ICA
cards.subtitle: 118 South 36th Street
cards.notes: Bring a friend to browse the galleries, then pause over one work and compare what each of you noticed before moving on.
cards.short_summary: A no-admission contemporary-art stop on Penn’s campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn identifies the Institute of Contemporary Art as free for all to engage with contemporary art.
cards.source_title: Penn Resources & Facilities Open to the Public
cards.access_notes: Penn’s public-resources page states that the ICA is free for all; check the ICA calendar before visiting.

cards.entity_name: To Secure These Rights: 150 Years of Women at Penn
cards.title: Explore 150 years of women at Penn
cards.subtitle: Van Pelt-Dietrich Library Center, first floor · Aug. 31–Dec. 11, 2026
cards.notes: Walk the display together and pick one photograph, document, or story to discuss on the way out of Van Pelt.
cards.short_summary: A public library exhibition on women’s history at Penn.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries says this exhibition is free and open to the public from August 31 through December 11, 2026.
cards.source_title: To Secure These Rights: 150 Years of Women at Penn
cards.access_notes: Visitors outside Penn need a current government- or school-issued photo ID for library access.

cards.title: Print a Declaration at Common Press
cards.subtitle: Fisher Fine Arts Library, Lower Level · through Dec. 18, 2026
cards.notes: Reserve a slot with a small group and take turns at the handpress while learning how the historic text was set in type.
cards.short_summary: A reservation-based public letterpress activity at Fisher.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries lists this Common Press opportunity among programs free of charge and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Reserve ahead; the page says Common Press is by appointment except during monthly open studios, and visitors should review access guidelines.

cards.title: Hear the campus-landscape book launch
cards.subtitle: Kleinman Energy Forum, Fisher Fine Arts Library · Sept. 10, 2026
cards.notes: Register with a classmate and listen for one campus landscape detail you want to find on a later walk.
cards.short_summary: A public conversation about Penn’s campus landscape.
cards.evidence_claim: Weitzman lists the Penn’s Sylvania book launch as free and open to the public with advance registration.
cards.access_notes: Advance registration is required; the event is scheduled for 6:30 p.m. on September 10, 2026.

cards.title: Catch Catherine Telford-Keogh’s artist talk
cards.subtitle: Institute of Contemporary Art · Oct. 22, 2026
cards.notes: Meet up before the talk, then use the walk back across campus to trade one question prompted by the presentation.
cards.short_summary: A free public visiting-artist lecture at the ICA.
cards.evidence_claim: Weitzman describes Catherine Telford-Keogh’s October 22, 2026 lecture at the ICA as free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The lecture is scheduled for 6 p.m.; the event page says registration information is forthcoming.

cards.entity_name: Anarchitecture After Everything: A Trans Manifesto
cards.title: Join the Anarchitecture book talk
cards.subtitle: Wolf Humanities Center location to be determined · Oct. 28, 2026
cards.notes: Go with someone curious about art or design, and stay for the Q&A after Jack Halberstam’s illustrated book talk.
cards.short_summary: A free public humanities talk with a Q&A.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wolf Humanities Center lists this October 28, 2026 book talk as free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Anarchitecture After Everything: A Trans Manifesto
cards.access_notes: Scheduled 5:30–7 p.m.; the Wolf Humanities Center lists the location as to be determined.

cards.title: Attend Rachel Kolb’s ASL and English forum
cards.subtitle: Wolf Humanities Center location to be determined · Nov. 11, 2026
cards.notes: Plan to arrive with a friend and stay for the discussion on communication, language, and lived experience after the talk.
cards.short_summary: A public forum presented in ASL with ASL/English interpretation.
cards.evidence_claim: The Wolf Humanities Center says Rachel Kolb’s November 11, 2026 forum is free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled 5:30–7:30 p.m.; registration and the final location are still forthcoming.

cards.entity_name: Common Press Workshops and Open Studios
cards.title: Try a free Common Press workshop
cards.subtitle: Common Press, Fisher Fine Arts Library
cards.notes: Watch the events calendar, reserve an eligible session, and make something together rather than just passing through the library.
cards.short_summary: Free public printmaking opportunities, with registration details on the calendar.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries states that Common Press opportunities are free of charge and open to all.
cards.access_notes: Check the event calendar and access guidelines; the studio is by appointment except for monthly open studio sessions.

cards.entity_name: Weitzman School Fine Arts Lecture Series
cards.title: Make a plan for a free visiting-artist lecture
cards.subtitle: Usually Institute of Contemporary Art, 118 South 36th Street
cards.notes: Choose a listed speaker with friends, arrive a few minutes early, and use the conversation afterward to unpack one idea from the lecture.
cards.short_summary: A public lecture series featuring artists, activists, writers, and other guests.
cards.evidence_claim: Weitzman states that all lectures in its Fine Arts Visiting Artist Lecture Series are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Confirm the speaker’s venue and time on the series page; the page notes that some lectures may be held outside the ICA.

cards.entity_name: Penn Libraries Public Events and Exhibitions
cards.title: Build a no-cost library culture night
cards.subtitle: Penn Libraries locations across campus
cards.notes: Pick an event or exhibition marked public, pair it with a stroll through the library displays, and check access details before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A rotating calendar of public library events, performances, workshops, and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: Penn Libraries says many of its events and exhibitions are open to the public and lists free workshops in its programming.
cards.access_notes: Select a listing explicitly marked free and open to the public; individual event pages provide registration and access requirements.
